canonical_title: HyperSeg: Patch-wise Hypernetwork for Real-time Semantic Segmentation
authors: Yuval Nirkin, Lior Wolf, Tal Hassner
paper_core_claims: HyperSeg uses a patch-wise hypernetwork that generates segmentation head weights conditioned on the input image patch.
The hypernetwork enables dynamic, input-dependent weight generation for real-time semantic segmentation.
The architecture achieves competitive accuracy with real-time performance by generating weights at the patch level.
function_concept_used_by_paper: Functions (segmentation models) are dynamically generated per input patch. The segmentation function is not fixed but is compiled on-the-fly based on the input.
representation_or_carrier: Dynamically generated segmentation head weights, conditioned on image patch features.
compiler_or_generator: The hypernetwork generates segmentation weights from encoder features. This is a concrete, input-conditioned compilation pipeline.
interpreter_or_runtime: The generated segmentation head processes the patch features to produce segmentation maps.
composition_rule: Patch-wise generation: different patches may receive different weight configurations. No formal composition algebra.
state_or_effect_model: Input-dependent weight generation. No formal state tracking.
validation_regime: Empirical: Cityscapes, Pascal Context, ADE20K semantic segmentation benchmarks.
limitations_and_failure_boundaries: No formal specification of what segmentation function is compiled.
No equivalence checking between generated models for different patches.
No effect tracking or state management.
source_specific_reasoning: S120-014 demonstrates input-conditioned weight generation for real-time segmentation. Strong evidence for N3 (Compiler) and N5 (Interpreter) with clear per-patch compilation. However, ephemeral artifacts, no formal spec, no equivalence, no versioning.
